title: Kozhikode Spices Limited — inventory valuation and revenue cut-off
narrative:
Kozhikode Spices Limited exports ground spice blends and holds both owned inventory and goods placed with distributors on consignment. The year-end is 31 March. The Financial Controller is finalising inventory valuation and revenue cut-off and has given you the schedules in Exhibits 1 and 2.

Inventory is measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value under Ind AS 2 / IAS 2. Revenue is recognised under Ind AS 115 / IFRS 15 when control transfers. Management has proposed recognising a bill-and-hold arrangement described in Exhibit 2 and is seeking confirmation that the criteria are met.

exhibits.label: Exhibit 2 — Revenue and cut-off items
exhibits.caption: Transactions under review

tasks.prompt: Calculate the total write-down to NRV required for inventory lines 1 and 4 combined.
tasks.hint: Whole dollars. Write down only where NRV is below cost.
tasks.explanation: Line 1: $120,000 - $95,000 = $25,000. Line 4: $45,000 - $40,000 = $5,000. Total write-down $30,000. Lines 2 and 3 need no write-down (NRV >= cost).

tasks.prompt: After the NRV adjustments and after removing the cost of consignment goods sold in March, what is the carrying amount of inventory that should appear on the 31 March statement of financial position?
tasks.hint: Start from the four lines' costs, adjust, then remove sold consignment cost.
tasks.explanation: Unadjusted costs $120k+$80k+$60k+$45k = $305,000. Less NRV write-downs $30,000 = $275,000. Less cost of consignment sold in March $22,000 = carrying amount $253,000. (Remaining consignment $58,000 stays in Kozhikode's inventory until sold to end customers.)

tasks.prompt: Complete the statement on consignment accounting.

fields.label: Goods on consignment at the distributor (unsold to end customers) are reported as inventory of
options: neither party until cash is remitted

fields.label: and revenue on the March consignment sales report should be recognised by Kozhikode of

tasks.explanation: Under a consignment arrangement control does not pass until sale to the end customer. Unsold consigned goods remain Kozhikode's inventory; the $35,000 sold in March is Kozhikode revenue (with related cost $22,000).

tasks.prompt: Which of the following support recognising revenue on bill-and-hold Order BH-17 at 31 March? Select all that apply.

options: The reason for the hold is substantive and requested by the customer.
The goods are separately identified as the customer's and ready for transfer.
Kozhikode retains the ability to redirect the goods to another customer if demand picks up.
The customer has accepted the billing and the related risks.
An invoice was issued before the reporting date.

tasks.explanation: IFRS 15 bill-and-hold criteria require a substantive customer-requested reason, separate identification, readiness for transfer, and that the entity cannot use the goods or redirect them. Issuing an invoice alone is not sufficient; redirectability would defeat the criteria.

tasks.prompt: For each shipment, decide whether revenue is recognised in the year ended 31 March.

items.text: Shipment S-904 (FOB shipping point, loaded 31 March)
Shipment S-911 (FOB destination, still in warehouse 31 March)
Consignment sales to end customers reported for March
Unsold consignment goods still at the distributor

zones.yes: Recognise revenue in year ended 31 March

tasks.explanation: FOB shipping point transfers control on loading — S-904 is March revenue. FOB destination waits for delivery — S-911 is April. Consignment revenue follows end-customer sales; unsold consignment is not revenue.

tasks.prompt: Calculate total revenue that should be recognised from Exhibit 2 items in the year ended 31 March (BH-17, S-904, S-911, consignment).
tasks.hint: Whole dollars. Apply the cut-off and bill-and-hold conclusions from prior tasks.
tasks.explanation: BH-17 $150,000 (criteria met) + S-904 $40,000 + consignment $35,000 = $225,000. S-911 $26,000 is excluded (FOB destination, not delivered).

tasks.prompt: If management refused the NRV write-down on line 1 only, by how much would pre-tax income for the year be overstated?
tasks.explanation: Omitting the $25,000 cardamom write-down overstates inventory and pre-tax income by $25,000. The $5,000 raw-pepper write-down is a separate line.
